data.title: True Digital Park’s “Hello, Connecting to New Possibilities” Wins Influencer Award
data.description: Reinforcing its role as a tech and startup ecosystem that connects people, businesses, and opportunities from around the world, True Digital Park, Southeast Asia’s largest tech and startup hub, has won the Best Property & Real Estate Influencer Campaign at the Thailand Influencer Awards 2026, recognising the success of its “Hello, Connecting to New Possibilities” campaign. Built around the simple yet powerful idea of “Hello” as the starting point for new connections, the campaign highlights how meaningful connections can open doors to new opportunities, support business growth, expand partnerships, and strengthen the technology community. It also reflects True Digital Park’s role as a hub that brings together people, businesses, technology, and new possibilities under the concept of “One Roof, All Possibilities”.

data.title: Thailand proud! Central celebrates Nene Royal — 1st Thai to win America’s Got Talent
data.description: Central Pattana Plc has joined Thailand in celebrating 16-year-old Phuket native Rattikan “Praew” Amloy, better known as Nene Royal, who made history as the first Thai winner of America’s Got Talent Season 21 (2026).

data.title: AIA Thailand Partners with Healthcare Accreditation Institute (Public Organization)
data.description: AIA Thailand has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Healthcare Accreditation Institute (Public Organization) to strengthen healthcare quality standards and enhance value-based healthcare service delivery across Thailand. The signing ceremony was attended by the executives, including Dr. Benjapol Engkaninan, Associate Director, Head of Health Strategy, AIA Thailand, and Dr. Piyawan Limpanyalert, CEO of the Healthcare Accreditation Institute (Public Organization).

data.title: Pope to speak on united Europe from French border town
data.description: METZ (FRANCE) - Pope Leo was to speak on Monday about the future of Europe and its integration, giving a distinctly political dimension to a landmark visit to France, which has sparked scenes of spiritual jubilation.

data.title: Big Bad Wolf Books' annual sale running now at Platinum Pop
data.description: Big Bad Wolf Books is marking a decade in Thailand with its biggest Bangkok book sale yet, turning more than 6,000m² across two floors of Platinum Pop, Ratchadamri Road, into a city-centre book hunt, daily from 10am to midnight from Friday to Oct 13.

data.title: Rapping for clean air
data.description: Eleven-year-old Aunna Tuamcharoen has allergies and takes medication most nights during the haze season. When she first tried to perform a new Unicef rap song that doubles as a breathing exercise, she managed only about half the target.

data.title: Down's artists on show at  '21/3 Extra Universe'
data.description: Moca Bangkok invites everyone to take a disguise and enter an abstract universe created by 50 artists with Down's syndrome during "21/3 Extra Universe", which is running until Oct 11.

data.title: Princess leads Thai dressage charge
data.description: TOKYO: Her Royal Highness Princess Sirivannavari Nariratana Rajakanya led Thailand's dressage team at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 as the riders concluded their dressage competition yesterday, with Nynn Puttisombat finishing sixth in the individual final at JRA Equestrian Park in Tokyo.

data.title: The American Beef Feast is back
data.description: Gourmet One, a leading importer and distributor of premium food products in Thailand, is bringing back the American Beef Feast for two months of premium US beef, from Thursday to Nov 30.

data.title: City Hall reports flooding on several streets
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration reported flood levels from 16 centimetres to 47cm deep on several streets on Monday morning.

data.title: Greece stun Klopp's Germany as Ireland show sorrow for Gaza
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Substitute Dimitrios Kourbelis gave Greece a shock 1-0 Nations League win away to Germany on Sunday as Ireland's players wore black armbands for their match against Israel.

data.title: Puripol's golden double act
data.description: Thailand's sprint sensation Puripol Boonson set the Nagoya track ablaze once more, scorching to men's 200m gold at the 2026 Asian Games in a continental record-equalling 19.88 seconds on Sunday.

data.title: Teerasak fires, Hudson gets his reward
data.description: Thailand opened their Fifa Asean Cup campaign in emphatic fashion, brushing aside Pakistan 4-0 at the Si Jalak Harupat Stadium on Saturday night, followed by confirmation from the Football Association of Thailand (FAT) that it had extended head coach Anthony Hudson's contract to February 2028.

data.title: Ireland beat Israel but no handshakes due to war in Gaza
data.description: DEBRECEN (HUNGARY) - Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in a Nations League clash on Sunday amid an eerie and sombre atmosphere that saw the Irish players wear black armbands over the war in Gaza.

data.title: Washington denounces Iran's truce proposal as 'cynical'
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - A top US official on Sunday dismissed a proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz presented by Iran as "cynical" and indicated it was a non-starter for Washington.

data.title: Food supplies 'still secure'
data.description: The government has warned consumers against panic buying and businesses against hoarding or price gouging as floods disrupt transport.

data.title: Govt moves to streamline provincial bureaucracy
data.description: The number of civil servants in provincial administration will be gradually reduced, with no new positions created from now on, Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt said on Sunday.

data.title: Thousands stranded by rising waters
data.description: Bangkok is stepping up safety measures in flooded communities after a 58-year-old woman was electrocuted, with thousands stranded amid dangerously high water.

data.title: Floods force extra holiday
data.description: The cabinet has declared Monday and Tuesday special public holidays in Bangkok and three neighbouring provinces to ease travel disruption and protect the public amid widespread flooding.

data.title: Support pours in for brothers forced to scavenge for food
data.description: The sight of two brothers searching rubbish bins for food at night in Bang Bua Thong, Nonthaburi, has prompted an outpouring of support after their story went viral.

data.title: City's main airport, THAI to work on flight delays
data.description: Suvarnabhumi Airport is working with Thai Airways (THAI) to resolve flight and baggage delays caused by flooding-related shortages of ground-handling staff.

data.title: Sondhi campaign off to slow start
data.description: Sondhi Limthongkul has returned to the political stage, but his latest mobilisation has yet to generate the mass response associated with his earlier campaigns.

data.title: Barcode claims put to test
data.description: The Constitutional Court is due to deliver its ruling on Monday on whether the use of barcodes and QR codes on ballot papers in the Feb 8 general election breached the constitutional requirement for voting to be secret.

data.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 8
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Russian strikes killed eight people across Ukraine a day after Moscow vowed to achieve its war aims "no matter the circumstances", authorities said Sunday.

data.title: UK village on edge over threats to air base in terror alert
data.description: CIRENCESTER (UNITED KINGDOM) - Residents in a bucolic corner of southwestern England said they were "spooked" by an air base used by the US military in its war against Iran as bomb experts descended on the area on Sunday.

data.title: Serbia's President Aleksandar Vucic announces resignation
data.description: BELGRADE - Serbia's long-time populist President Aleksandar Vucic resigned Sunday to run for prime minister in October snap elections after nearly two years of student-led protests that had been pressing for just such a poll.
